response.rationale: R5 is the strongest because the telemetry directly shows ventricular ectopy triggering VF, and the extensive negative workup (normal echo, MRI, coronary angiogram, no electrolyte derangements, negative toxicology, negative genetic testing, absent Brugada and early repolarization patterns) supports idiopathic ventricular fibrillation as a diagnosis of exclusion. R1 (CPVT) is plausible given PVC-triggered polymorphic VT, but lacks genetic confirmation and an explicit adrenergic trigger, and the presence of VF with culprit PVC ablation favors IVF.

rejected.why: QTc 443/433 ms is not diagnostic of long QT syndrome, and genetic testing was negative.
High precordial ECG did not demonstrate Brugada pattern, directly contradicting Brugada syndrome.
Follow-up ECG showed absence of early repolarization pattern, excluding early repolarization syndrome.
CPVT is less likely because genetic testing identified no pathogenic variants and no exercise or emotional trigger was documented; VF and ablation of culprit PVCs favor idiopathic VF.
